newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Retailer F.J. Benjamin bullish on Asia Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Retailer F.J. Benjamin bullish on Asia Pacific.

text.p: Singapore fashion retailer and distributor F.J. Benjamin sees higher revenue from the Asia Pacific region and is bullish on Singapore despite a retail slump.

"Currently 56 percent of our turnover comes from the region and because of the growing economies in the Asia Pacific" that is expected to increase, president and chief executive officer Frank Benjamin said.
He was speaking to reporters at a briefing on the company's initial public offering, launched on Tuesday.
The company has announced an offer of 50 million new shares at Singapore S$0.80 (US$0.57) each, of which 10 million shares set aside for placement have already been fully taken up.

"We see that the business in Singapore as well will grow. But we feel that spreading ourselves into the major cities in the Asia Pacific will logically give us a higher turnover in the region than we will have in Singapore," Benjamin said.
For the next three to five years the company would be looking to reach a level of 65-70 percent of turnover from outside Singapore, he said.
For the financial year ended June 30, 1996, it recorded a net profit of S$10.9 million on a turnover of S$255.07 million.
The company's business in Singapore had not suffered despite losses by major department stores because it was a niche player, Benjamin said.
He said the company would still focus on the tourist market in Singapore, where he expected a tourism plan to boost visitor numbers.
Singapore contributed more than 43.7 percent or S$111.4 million to the group's revenue in fiscal 1996 and over 70 percent or S$11.38 million to pretax profit, which totalled S$15.91 million.

"Notwithstanding the (upward) trend of the Singapore dollar and not withstanding the fact that there has been a drop in tourism spending per head, we've noticed that for brands which are very popular and much in demand, the sales have gone up," said Benjamin.
For its overseas markets, Benjamin said the U.S. clothing and accessories Guess? label had been the major contributor.
"We used Guess? which has become a phenomenal success in the Far East markets to establish our businesses in the region at a very fast pace."

However, no single brand will contribute more than 30 percent of group turnover, he added. Besides Guess, the group retails such brands as Gucci, Fendi, Hunting World, bedding brand Sheridan and its own clothing brand Rachel B. It also distributes fashion wear and accessories and has some business from export, licensing and design.
